props.title: Resident Evil
props.initialSlug: Special forces battle zombies in secret lab nightmare

sections.content: Resident Evil (2002) launched Hollywood's most successful video game film franchise by smartly blending zombie horror with slick action sequences. Director Paul W.S. Anderson created a more contained story than the sprawling games, focusing on an amnesiac security officer (Milla Jovovich) trapped in an underground facility. The film established a template that later video game adaptations like Silent Hill (2006) and Doom (2005) would follow - taking core elements from the source material while crafting an original narrative. While purists criticized departures from the games, the film's mix of undead threats, corporate conspiracy, and memorable set pieces like the laser hallway sequence proved commercially successful.

sections.content: The franchise's evolution mirrors broader shifts in action-horror cinema of the 2000s. While the original maintained claustrophobic tension reminiscent of Aliens (1986), later entries expanded into post-apocalyptic territory following trends set by 28 Days Later (2002) and Dawn of the Dead (2004). The series increasingly emphasized elaborate action sequences and superhuman abilities, moving away from survival horror toward superhero-adjacent sci-fi action, particularly evident in Resident Evil: Retribution (2012).

Milla Jovovich's Alice became one of the few enduring female action heroes of the era, alongside characters like Underworld's (2003) Selene. The films consistently delivered stylized violence and ambitious set pieces, even as plot coherence diminished. This approach influenced later video game adaptations like Monster Hunter (2020), which similarly prioritized spectacle over strict game accuracy. SUBHEAD: Impact on Video Game Adaptations

sections.content: The financial success of Resident Evil helped legitimize video game adaptations in Hollywood, paving the way for bigger budgets and more ambitious projects. While critically divisive, the franchise demonstrated that game adaptations could sustain multiple sequels, influencing productions like Silent Hill: Revelation (2012) and Tomb Raider (2018). The 2022 reboot Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City attempted to hew closer to the games' horror roots, showing the lasting influence of the original's premise.
